Subject: Pilot launch: request for temporary priority window (Sept 20)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the run-through earlier. We’re on track to start our integration pilot the week of Sept 20. Based on our load tests, the first day will include a concentrated ingestion window (08:00–12:00 PT) where we’ll spike to ~3.2x our steady-state token rate for a three-hour stretch.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary priority window (throttling/fairness carveout) for Sept 20, 08:00–12:00 PT to keep response latencies under 400ms?
- We’ve attached a traffic projection CSV to help sizing.

We’re happy to sign a short MOU or add a one-off addendum for billing and SLAs. If you need additional telemetry during the window (traces, token counts), we can pull those on our side as well.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

Samir Patel
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Health

Samir — thanks for the context and the projection. I’ve looped in Ben (ops) and Kimberly (commercial/contracting) to scope the request. Quick confirmations we need before I commit to a window:
- Exact timezone for the spike (you said PT — we’ll assume PDT for Sept 20).
- Expected token/sec at 08:00–09:00 and the 3-hour average expected.
- Whether this window must be reserved across all models or a single model/route.

Ben — can you review whether we can offer a temporary priority lane (token pool + relaxed fairness policy) for a 4-hour reserve? If so, we should document the operational triggers and fallback behavior.

Kimberly — if Acme can sign a short MOU and accept a one-time usage uplift, are there any standard clauses you want in the addendum? I’ll propose a draft once we confirm the technical size.

I’ll coordinate and aim to get back with a firm proposal by EOD tomorrow.

—Mateo

On Thu, Sep 2, 2026 at 2:44 PM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben — can you review whether we can offer a temporary priority lane (token pool + relaxed fairness policy) for a 4-hour reserve? If so, we should document the operational triggers and fallback behavior.

Happy to take this. Quick ops read:
- We can carve out a short-lived token pool scoped to Acme’s account for a hard window (start/end timestamps). That pool routes to a reserved execution queue with higher priority scheduling.
- Constraints: we can guarantee a latency SLO only if pool consumption remains within the attached projection tolerance (+/-15%). If actual ingestion exceeds the projection by >25% we’ll kick in automatic throttling back to standard fairness.
- We’ll also require that Acme enable our lightweight runbook agent (read-only telemetry) so we can surface tail latencies in real time.

Operational terms I propose to include in the MOU:
1) Effective window: 2026-09-20T15:00:00Z — 2026-09-20T19:00:00Z (08:00–12:00 PT).
2) Token pool size: 1.5M tokens for the window (exhaustion triggers throttling).
3) Latency target during window: p95 < 400ms; no availability SLA change outside the reserved pool.
4) Overrun policy: consumption >1.25x projection -> automatic revert to fairness queue; ops will notify within 10 minutes.

If the customer signs up to those terms and enables the runbook agent, ops can implement the pool and validation checks.

—Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks — excited to get this pilot rolling.
